title: One-level lifting of filtered relations among projective order forms
statement:
Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], $r\ge0$, and $B=k[X_0,\ldots,X_r]$ with the grading by total degree [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring, def-pc-standard-graded-algebra]. Let $\mathfrak p\subset k[t_1,\ldots,t_r]$ be a prime ideal, $L=k[t_1,\ldots,t_r]_{\mathfrak p}$, and $N=\mathfrak pL$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. Write $\delta(f)=f(1,t_1,\ldots,t_r)/1$, $U_d=\{f\in B_d:\delta(f)\in N^d\}$, and $U=\bigoplus_{d\ge0}U_d$. For any ideal $J$, write $\operatorname{ord}_J(h)=\sup\{n:h\in J^n\}$, with value $\infty$ for membership in every power. Let $\widehat L=\varprojlim_nL/N^n$ be the completion [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion] and $\widehat N=N\widehat L$. Let $b\ge0$ and let nonzero $\phi_j\in U_{e_j}$ have degrees $e_j\ge1$ for $1\le j\le b$; put $\theta_j=\delta(\phi_j)\in\widehat L$. For any integer $q\ge0$ and $u_j\in\widehat L$ satisfying
$$u_j\in\widehat N^{\max(0,q-e_j)}\quad(1\le j\le b),\qquad \sum_ju_j\theta_j\in\widehat N^{q+1},$$
there exist $v_j\in\widehat L$ such that
$$\sum_jv_j\theta_j=0,\qquad u_j-v_j\in\widehat N^{\max(0,q+1-e_j)}\quad(1\le j\le b).$$
The empty family is allowed. Thus the assertion lifts a relation at a single filtration level to an exact relation; its coefficients are in the completion, and are not required to be homogeneous polynomials.

source.place: External source read online: Hironaka, Certain numerical characters of singularities, J. Math. Kyoto Univ. 10-1 (1970), Lemma 17, pp.172-173, exact-relation consequence, with its t-double-prime equal to q and valuation inequalities interpreted integrally. https://scispace.com/pdf/certain-numerical-characters-of-singularities-18d51ii5bz.pdf. Archival copy WANTED; the ILO document is the VIII 2.3.13 ancestor motivation only. No Stacks tag states this specialized assertion.

proof.text: If $b=0$, take the empty tuple. If $q=0$, take every $v_j=0$: since $e_j\ge1$, every required exponent $\max(0,1-e_j)$ is zero. Assume $q\ge1$. Let $A=\{j:e_j\le q\}$. For $j\notin A$ set $v_j=0$; their approximation condition is again vacuous and $u_j\theta_j\in\widehat N^{e_j}\subseteq\widehat N^{q+1}$. Hence $\sum_{j\in A}u_j\theta_j\in\widehat N^{q+1}$. If $A$ is empty this already finishes the proof.

source.place: Agent reconstruction of the exact-relation consequence of Hironaka (1970), Lemma 17, pp.172–173, read online at https://scispace.com/pdf/certain-numerical-characters-of-singularities-18d51ii5bz.pdf; archival original WANTED. ILO VIII 2.3.13 is ancestor motivation only.

proof.text: A field is Noetherian: an ideal is zero or, on containing a nonzero $a$, contains $a^{-1}a=1$. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian], $k[t_1,\ldots,t_r]$ is Noetherian, and by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-noetherian] so is $L$. Thus $N$ is finitely generated, by [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. This verifies the hypothesis for the completion quotient theorem used next.

Write $\iota:L\to\widehat L$. Extension of ideals commutes with products (expand finite sums of products), so $N^m\widehat L=\widehat N^m$. By [lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-mod-power], choose $\beta_j\in L$ representing the $(q+1)$-st coordinate of $u_j$ for $j\in A$. Then $\iota(\beta_j)-u_j\in\widehat N^{q+1}$. Put $m_j=q-e_j\ge0$. If $m_j>0$, the $m_j$-th coordinate of $u_j$ is zero, so compatibility of coordinates gives $\beta_j\in N^{m_j}$; if $m_j=0$ this holds automatically. Also $s=\sum_{j\in A}\beta_j\delta(\phi_j)$ maps into $\widehat N^{q+1}$. Its $(q+1)$-st coordinate is $s\bmod N^{q+1}$ by the same cited theorem, whence $s\in N^{q+1}$.

Apply [lem-trf-projective-order-leading-syzygies] to the finite nonempty family indexed by $A$, with its parameter $e=q$, degrees $d_j=e_j$, and coefficients $\beta_j$. All degrees lie in $[1,q]$; membership in $U_{e_j}$ is unchanged, and Step 3 verifies both coefficient and sum hypotheses in $L$. Obtain $V,h_v,a_v,C_{vj}$ with $\sum_{j\in A}C_{vj}\phi_j=0$ and $\beta_j-\sum_va_v\delta(C_{vj})\in N^{q-e_j+1}$ for each $j\in A$.

source.place: Agent reconstruction of the exact-relation consequence of Hironaka (1970), Lemma 17, pp.172–173, read online at https://scispace.com/pdf/certain-numerical-characters-of-singularities-18d51ii5bz.pdf; archival original WANTED. ILO VIII 2.3.13 is ancestor motivation only.

proof.text: For $j\in A$, define $v_j=\sum_v\iota(a_v)\iota(\delta(C_{vj}))$. Apply the evaluation homomorphism and then $\iota$ to each polynomial identity from Step 4; distributing the finite sums gives $\sum_{j\in A}v_j\theta_j=\sum_v\iota(a_v)\iota(\delta(\sum_{j\in A}C_{vj}\phi_j))=0$. Moreover $u_j-v_j=(u_j-\iota(\beta_j))+\iota(\beta_j-\sum_va_v\delta(C_{vj}))$ lies in $\widehat N^{q-e_j+1}$, since $q+1\ge q-e_j+1$. Together with the zero choices outside $A$, these are exactly the asserted equality and all the required congruences.

lean.statement: theorem projective_order_filtered_syzygy_lifting {k : Type u} [Field k] (r b q : ℕ) (p : PrimeSpectrum (MvPolynomial {i : Fin (r + 1) // i ≠ 0} k)) (e : Fin b → ℕ) (φ : Fin b → MvPolynomial (Fin (r + 1)) k) (he : ∀ j : Fin b, 1 ≤ e j) (hφ_ne : ∀ j : Fin b, φ j ≠ 0) (hφ : ∀ j : Fin b, InOrderSpace r p (e j) (φ j)) (u : Fin b → AdicCompletion (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal (Localization.AtPrime p.asIdeal)) (Localization.AtPrime p.asIdeal)) (hu : ∀ j : Fin b, u j ∈ (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal (Localization.AtPrime p.asIdeal)).map (algebraMap _ _) ^ (q - e j)) (hsum : (∑ j : Fin b, u j * algebraMap (Localization.AtPrime p.asIdeal) _ (algebraMap _ (Localization.AtPrime p.asIdeal) (MvPolynomial.dehomogenizeX k 0 (φ j)))) ∈ (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal (Localization.AtPrime p.asIdeal)).map (algebraMap _ _) ^ (q + 1)) : ∃ v : Fin b → AdicCompletion (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal (Localization.AtPrime p.asIdeal)) (Localization.AtPrime p.asIdeal), (∑ j : Fin b, v j * algebraMap (Localization.AtPrime p.asIdeal) _ (algebraMap _ (Localization.AtPrime p.asIdeal) (MvPolynomial.dehomogenizeX k 0 (φ j)))) = 0 ∧ ∀ j : Fin b, u j - v j ∈ (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal (Localization.AtPrime p.asIdeal)).map (algebraMap _ _) ^ (q + 1 - e j)
